summary: Three decided government actions this week have clean revenue mechanisms into the universe: a dated DGFT export ban on lithium-ion battery black mass (10 Nov) that locks feedstock for domestic recyclers, a 64%-larger Rs 62,370 crore Cabinet fertiliser subsidy for the Rabi season (11 Nov), and a confirmed $659mn Paras-BroadPak OSAT packaging facility that the semis map is missing. Meanwhile Hormuz tanker/LNG disruption has flipped the energy-security trade from upstream-tailwind to refiner/shipper-tailwind-plus-upstream-headwind, and the Jensen Huang/Nvidia-driven chip-stock rout keeps the EMS memory-cost headwind alive rather than resolved.

themes.name: Critical minerals & battery recycling
themes.thesis: A dated export prohibition on lithium-ion battery black mass forces domestic scrap generators to sell feedstock to Indian recyclers instead of exporting it, lowering their input costs and securing capacity utilisation; a parallel NMDC-Rosatom lithium exploration talk adds a longer-dated supply-side option.

drivers.what: DGFT Notification 49/2026-27 prohibits export of lithium-ion battery black mass (HS 85491400), effective immediately
NMDC in talks with Russia's Rosatom to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities

beneficiaries.mechanism: Lead-acid/lithium battery recycler whose core feedstock is black mass; export ban guarantees domestic supply and improves margin via lower input cost.
beneficiaries.evidence: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2335019&lang=1&reg=3

beneficiaries.mechanism: Metal and battery-material recycler; same feedstock-lock mechanism as Gravita.
